brief_angle: Inside a mirrored crystal sauna — a hard-faceted steel shell wrapped in steam and a heat source — does the acoustic space stay legible enough to move through, or does the geometry collapse into a wash a blind body cannot read; and if it does collapse, is that a defect of the room or the actual point of a sauna, a space designed to be un-navigated?
notes: The Finnish swimmer never actually speaks. 'She told them she comes precisely to lose her bearings' and 'A sauna where you always know exactly where the door is, she said, has failed at the one thing a sauna is for' are reported speech with no quotation marks, delivered secondhand through Bigert & Bergström, and shaped exactly to serve the turn the argument needs. Get her real words inside actual quotation marks — ideally something rougher than the thesis wants — or the piece is a monologue in a sealed room. And when she does speak, hers should stay the sharpest line in the piece; right now the narrator tops her twice in the paragraphs that follow.

Two verdict-sentences over budget. 'But a sauna is not a station.' stands as its own single-sentence paragraph, and 'The wash took the geometry. It did not take the people.' is a second full epigram three paragraphs later. Keep 'The wash took the geometry. It did not take the people.' — it's doing real work in the piece's most important paragraph — and flatten 'But a sauna is not a station' into the top of the following paragraph as plain prose.

Protect the she-and-I comparative in the paragraph beginning 'There are rooms whose whole job is to stop the reading' — 'She has spent her life being able to see the door and needs somewhere to put that down. I have spent mine unable to see it and needing everywhere else to give it back.' That parallel carries the whole argument without commentary and is the best thing in the draft; whatever gets moved in revision, that stays. But cut the sentence that introduces the surrounding section, 'I want to be exact about what I could and couldn't do in there.' — it announces the precision instead of performing it. Start straight at 'I could not map the shell.'
